# SEARCH-IN Product Facts

Official URL: https://searchin.pages.dev/
Publisher: promptedteam
Distribution: https://github.com/promptedteam/searchin
Current public Windows release: 2.1.0.104
Pricing: The desktop app is free to use. Optional third-party AI usage can have separate fees and limits.
Source availability: Closed source. The public GitHub repository contains downloads, documentation, demo media, website files, and updater metadata, not the application or engine source.

## What SEARCH-IN Does

SEARCH-IN is local desktop search software, not an internet search engine.
Files mode finds filenames and paths in the included engine's catalog. Directory scope and file-type filters help narrow the result set.
In-File mode searches text prepared by the Content Indexer. Match snippets help identify relevant documents. Both modes share an embedded preview pane.
The engine must run for its search catalog. The Content Indexer window need not remain open merely to search text already indexed.
Filename discovery does not imply document text has been indexed. A file must be inside the content-index scope and finish local extraction before its available text can be searched in In-File.

## Local Indexing and Optional OCR

Local extraction runs before optional AI OCR. Documents with accessible text do not need an AI call just to become searchable.
Scanned pages and images need optical character recognition to make visible lettering searchable. Eligible unreadable files can appear as AI Pending.
Users choose a supported vision provider, configure their own credentials, review pending files, and approve the AI run. Only then are eligible files sent to that provider.
AI providers have separate pricing, allowances, rate limits, and privacy terms. Multiple keys can be stored per provider, rotated on rate limits, and paused during cooldowns.
Optional AI OCR is not a promise of semantic chat or unrestricted AI access to every local file.

## Preview Coverage and Limits

Preview categories include PDF, Word OpenXML, formatted RTF, basic Excel worksheet values, basic PowerPoint slide text, common images, supported PSD composites and PDF-compatible AI files, text/code/configuration, Markdown, subtitles, archive metadata, read-only binary hex, supported audio/video, EPUB, CBZ/CBR, OBJ/STL/FBX geometry, MusicXML/MXL, and font specimens.
Complex Word layout is approximate. Excel formulas/charts and full PowerPoint presentations are not reproduced. Media support depends on installed Windows/WebView2 codecs. Scanned images do not become searchable merely by displaying their preview.
RAW, HEIC, TIFF, EPS, MOBI/AZW, and legacy Office renderers are not bundled. Installed Windows preview handlers may add compatibility. The entire QuickLook plugin ecosystem is not included.

## Supported Platforms and Installation

Available now: Windows 10 and Windows 11, x64.
Required runtimes: Microsoft .NET 10 Desktop Runtime (x64) and Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime.
Windows Setup installs the app and its included engine. Portable ZIP must be fully extracted before running SearchIn.exe.
For an offline PC, obtain the official standalone Microsoft runtime installers using another PC first. The small WebView2 bootstrapper needs internet and is not the offline runtime.
Application packages are currently unsigned. Windows may display a publisher or SmartScreen warning. Release SHA-256 checksums are available.
macOS: Coming soon as a planned direction. No public build or announced release date.
Linux: Coming soon as a planned direction. No public build or announced release date.
Do not describe macOS or Linux as currently supported, and do not invent download links for them.

## Tutorials

Four one-minute 1920x1080 captioned videos are embedded at https://searchin.pages.dev/#guides in a two-column grid on desktop and mobile.
The setup chapter is a labeled simulation, not a recorded runtime installation. It does not yet contain the live GitHub download segment.
The indexing, filename search, and In-File/preview chapters show the real app using synthetic files, fictional paths, scripted pointers, and on-screen guidance.
The AI demonstration uses an invalid demo credential and makes no provider request.

## Privacy and Updates

Local indexing, filename search, document-content search, and previews run on the user's computer. Optional AI provider processing requires user approval.
Provider credentials are protected for the Windows account and stored outside the installation directory. Public releases do not contain user credentials, databases, or private captures.
The website has no sign-in or analytics scripts.
SEARCH-IN 2.1.0.104 supports in-app update checking and downloading with a quiet download indicator. Users choose when to review and install an update.
LOCALOCR 1.x is a separate installation. SEARCH-IN does not silently migrate or delete its databases or credentials.

## Comparison With Other Search Apps

The landing page includes a source-linked workflow comparison with Everything, Listary, and Windows Search. Vendor descriptions refer to their official documentation, checked 19 October 2026, and may vary by version, edition, plugins, and configuration.
Everything emphasizes filename/folder search and search functions; its documentation also describes content searches. Listary emphasizes file search, app launching, and Open/Save folder switching. Windows Search indexes names, properties, and supported contents according to its locations and file-type settings.
SEARCH-IN's emphasized combination is a filename catalog, a dedicated document-content index, Match snippets, shared embedded previews, and optional approved AI OCR with provider/key control.
This comparison is not a claim that all competing products lack those features. There is no comparative speed, memory, or accuracy benchmark and no promise that SEARCH-IN is universally better.

## Roadmap

Directions include continued performance work, more reliable document previews, the LOCALTOOL taskbar companion in development, an optional server workflow under exploration, and future macOS/Linux platform work.
These are plans and areas to explore, not a claim that all are available. No release dates are promised.

This text is a supplemental product overview for readers and automated tools. It does not guarantee search indexing, AI citations, or rankings. Use the official release notes to verify shipped versions.
